rule: Seeded rule-list generator. One hill-based heightfield is normalised to 0-1000; ordered height bands (first match wins) label landforms; lakes are a fall-off spread seeded from high ground and rivers are a downhill-limited depth-first search to water or the edge; a second heightfield with ordered converters (height, temperature and terrain ranges) re-labels flat ground; castles are a spacing-and-terrain scan with a ranking; roads are A* over a per-terrain cost table; villages are a jittered grid with a rating-plus-neighbour-count picker. The whole job retries on failure, RNG advances across tries, and the schema types every row.
keep: ordered rule lists with first-match-wins for landforms and converters
seeded RNG per job, with bounded retries that advance the same RNG
river that flows downhill with a per-step uphill allowance, ending in water or off-map
lake as fall-off spread with a halving chance per ring
roads as cheapest path over a per-terrain cost table, bridges where water is crossed
village rating as base weight plus neighbour terrain counts
schema-typed rows for every generator table
change: rename river_frequency to river_uphill and lake_size to lake_fall_off (names are wrong in the donor)
validate that height and converter rows are sorted, or reject shadowed rows at load
add a walk-path check between spawn anchors; the donor drops failed roads silently
jitter villages in two axes (the donor reuses one offset for x and y)
make the castle choice explicit (the donor comment says random, the code is a deterministic scan)
do not expose a reroll-until-balanced note to players; check fairness on the server
let a zone carry several anchor kinds (the donor reads one castle rule per map)
look_test: Six zone seeds from one family row, rendered top-down at 375 px, side by side with the river rule switched off. Dom checks that each reads as a place (a lake or river, a road between two spawn points, at least three villages near water).
